content.raw_text: 从那一天起，孙悟空每天都和祖师一起学习。他在山洞里住了七年。第七年的一天，菩提祖师对孙悟空说，“在我的学校里有三百六十种不一样的办法。每种办法都能带你走向智慧。你想学哪一种？”

sentences.text: 从那一天起，孙悟空每天都和祖师一起学习。
sentences.translation: Since that day, Sun Wukong studied with his master every day.
sentences.explanation: The structure '每天都' emphasizes the frequency of the action, meaning 'every day' or 'always'.

sentences.text: 他在山洞里住了七年。
sentences.translation: He lived in a cave for seven years.
sentences.explanation: The structure '在...里' is used to indicate location, in this case, '在山洞里' means 'in the cave'. The particle '了' is used to indicate the completion of an action, in this case, '住了' means 'lived'.

sentences.text: 第七年的一天，菩提祖师对孙悟空说，“在我的学校里有三百六十种不一样的办法。
sentences.translation: One day in the seventh year, Patriarch Bodhi said to Sun Wukong, "In my school, there are three hundred and sixty different methods."
sentences.explanation: This sentence introduces the concept of different methods or techniques in a school setting. The structure '有...种...' is commonly used to express the existence of various types or kinds of something.

sentences.text: 每种办法都能带你走向智慧。
sentences.translation: Every method can lead you to wisdom.
sentences.explanation: The structure '每种...都能' is a common way to express 'every... can' in Chinese.

sentences.text: 你想学哪一种？
sentences.translation: Which one do you want to learn?
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure in Chinese is Subject + Verb + Object. In this sentence, the question word '哪' is used to ask 'which kind'.
The sentence ends with a closing quotation mark.

content.raw_text: “祖师让我学什么我就学什么，”孙悟空回答说。

sentences.text: “祖师让我学什么我就学什么，”孙悟空回答说。
sentences.translation: The Patriarch lets me learn whatever I want to learn,
sentences.explanation: In this sentence, the structure 孙悟空回答说 is used to indicate that Sun Wukong replied. The repetition of 学什么我就学什么 emphasizes the idea of learning whatever he wants.

content.raw_text: 菩提祖师告诉孙悟空三百六十种办法中的每一种。他说了很长时间。每次菩提祖师说一种办法，孙悟空就会问，“如果我学这种办法，我会成为神仙吗？”每次祖师都回答，“不会。”然后每次孙悟空说，“那我就不学这种办法。”

sentences.text: 菩提祖师告诉孙悟空三百六十种办法中的每一。
sentences.translation: Bodhi Patriarch told Sun Wukong each of the three hundred and sixty methods.
sentences.explanation: This sentence introduces a list of methods or ways that the Bodhi Patriarch told Sun Wukong about. The structure '每一种' means 'each one' or 'every kind'.

sentences.text: 他说了很长时间。
sentences.translation: He spoke for a long time.
sentences.explanation: The structure '说了' indicates that the action of speaking has been completed. The word '很' is used to intensify the adjective '长', meaning 'very long'.

sentences.text: 每次菩提祖师说一种办法，孙悟空就会问，“如果我学这种办法，我会成为神仙吗？
sentences.translation: Every time Bodhi Ancestor speaks of a method, Sun Wukong will ask, 'If I learn this method, will I become a god?'
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure involves a conditional question where Sun Wukong is inquiring about becoming a god if he learns a specific method.

sentences.text: ”每次祖师都回答，“不会。
sentences.translation: Every time the ancestor would answer, "I don't know."
sentences.explanation: The tricky part here is the use of "都" which indicates that the ancestor always responds in the same way, and the phrase "不会" which means "I don't know" in this context.

sentences.text: ”然后每次孙悟空说，“那我就不学这种办法。
sentences.translation: Then every time Sun Wukong said, 'Then I won't learn this method.'
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure '那我就不' is a common way to express 'then I won't' in Chinese.
The sentence is a polite way of asking someone to proceed to the next step.

content.raw_text: 菩提祖师很生气，对孙悟空喊，“你这只猴子！我已经告诉你很多能走向智慧的办法，但是你什么都不想要，什么都不想学。”他在孙悟空头上打了三下。然后他把手放在身体后面，走进他的房间，关上了门。

sentences.text: 菩提祖师很生气，对孙悟空喊，“你这只猴子！
sentences.translation: The Patriarch Bodhi was very angry and shouted at Sun Wukong, 'You, this monkey!
sentences.explanation: The sentence introduces the Patriarch Bodhi expressing anger towards Sun Wukong, calling him a monkey. The use of '对' indicates the action of shouting 'at' someone.

sentences.text: 我已经告诉你很多能走向智慧的办法，但是你什么都不想要，什么都不想学。
sentences.translation: I have already told you many ways to achieve wisdom, but you don't want anything, you don't want to learn anything.
sentences.explanation: The structure '什么都不' is used to emphasize the negation, meaning 'not anything/everything'.

sentences.text: ”他在孙悟空头上打了三下。
sentences.translation: He hit Sun Wukong on the head three times.
sentences.explanation: The structure '在...上' is used to indicate the location where an action takes place. The character '了' is used to indicate the completion of an action.

sentences.text: 然后他把手放在身体后面，走进他的房间，关上了门。
sentences.translation: Then he put his hand behind his body, walked into his room, and closed the door.
sentences.explanation: The structure '把...放在...' is a common way to express 'put...in...' in Chinese.

content.raw_text: 其他学生听到这些，都很生气，因为孙悟空让祖师生气。但是孙悟空一点儿不生气也没有不开心。他认为祖师告诉了他一个秘密。因为祖师在他的头上打了三下，他认为这意思是“等到三更”的时候，也就是从晚上十一点开始。祖师把手放在身体后面，他认为这意思是“从后门进我的房间，我可以教你。”

sentences.text: 其他学生听到这些，都很生气，因为孙悟空让祖师生气。
sentences.translation: Other students heard this and were all very angry because Sun Wukong made the patriarch angry.
sentences.explanation: The structure '因为...所以...' (because...therefore...) is commonly used in Chinese to indicate cause and effect relationships.

sentences.text: 但是孙悟空一点儿不生气也没有不开心。
sentences.translation: But Sun Wukong was not angry at all and not unhappy.
sentences.explanation: The structure '一点儿不' is used to emphasize the negation, meaning 'not at all'.

sentences.text: 他认为祖师告诉了他一个秘密。
sentences.translation: He thought the patriarch had told him a secret.
sentences.explanation: The structure '告诉了他' indicates that the patriarch told him something, with the particle '了' indicating the completion of the action.

sentences.text: 因为祖师在他的头上打了三下，他认为这意思是“等到三更”的时候，也就是从晚上十一点开始。
sentences.translation: Because the Patriarch hit him on the head three times, he thought it meant 'wait until the third watch of the night,' which is from eleven o'clock at night.
sentences.explanation: The sentence introduces a cultural reference to the concept of 'the third watch of the night,' which refers to a specific time period in ancient Chinese timekeeping.

sentences.text: 祖师把手放在身体后面，他认为这意思是“从后门进我的房间，我可以教你。
sentences.translation: The patriarch put his hand behind his body, thinking this meant 'enter my room from the back door, I can teach you.'
sentences.explanation: The sentence contains a complex structure where the patriarch interprets a gesture as an invitation to enter his room from the back door for a teaching session.

words.definition: particle used to indicate the object of a verb

sentences.explanation: The sentence contains a closing quotation mark and an ellipsis, indicating a continuation or omission of text.

content.raw_text: 所以那天晚上刚到三更，孙悟空走出房间，来到外面。他走到后门，门开着，他走进去。祖师正在床上睡觉。孙悟空就坐下来等祖师醒来。

sentences.text: 所以那天晚上刚到三更，孙悟空走出房间，来到外面。
sentences.translation: So that night, just past midnight, Sun Wukong walked out of the room and came outside.
sentences.explanation: The structure 刚...就 (just...then) is commonly used in Chinese to indicate that one action immediately follows another.

sentences.text: 他走到后门，门开着，他走进去。
sentences.translation: He walked to the back door, the door was open, and he walked in.
sentences.explanation: In Chinese, the verb '走' (walk) is often used to indicate movement towards a location. The structure 'Verb + 到' indicates reaching a destination. The structure 'Verb + 进去' indicates entering a place.

sentences.text: 祖师正在床上睡觉。
sentences.translation: The patriarch is sleeping in bed.
sentences.explanation: The tricky grammar structure here is the use of the word '正在' before the verb, indicating the action is currently taking place. '床上' is a prepositional phrase meaning 'in bed'.

sentences.text: 孙悟空就坐下来等祖师醒来。
sentences.translation: Sun Wukong sat down to wait for his master to wake up.
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure is Subject + Verb + Object. The word '就' here indicates a sequence of actions, meaning 'then' or 'just'. '等' is followed by the action being waited for.

content.raw_text: 当祖师醒来的时候，他看见孙悟空，笑着说，“你这猴子，你为什么在这儿？”

sentences.text: 当祖师醒来的时候，他看见孙悟空，笑着说，“你这猴子，你为什么在这儿？
sentences.translation: When the Patriarch woke up, he saw Sun Wukong and said with a smile, 'You monkey, why are you here?'
sentences.explanation: The sentence contains a possessive particle '的' to indicate possession, and the structure '为什么' means 'why'.
The sentence ends with a closing quotation mark.

content.raw_text: “祖师，”孙悟空说，“昨天你告诉了我一个秘密，你要我等到三更，然后经过后门到你的房间。现在我在这里，请教我长生的秘密。”

sentences.text: “祖师，”孙悟空说，“昨天你告诉了我一个秘密，你要我等到三更，然后经过后门到你的房间。
sentences.translation: Ancestor,
sentences.explanation: The sentence contains a complex structure involving reported speech and instructions, which may be challenging for intermediate learners.

words.definition: particle indicating completion of an action

sentences.text: 现在我在这里，请教我长生的秘密。
sentences.translation: Now I am here, seeking the secret of eternal life.
sentences.explanation: The structure '请教我' means 'seek advice from me'. The term '长生' refers to the concept of eternal life or immortality.
This sentence seems to be incomplete, as it starts with a closing quotation mark without a corresponding opening quotation mark.

content.raw_text: 菩提祖师在孙悟空耳边说了一首诗，诗里有长生的秘密。当然，我不能告诉你这首诗是什么，因为它是一个秘密。

sentences.text: 菩提祖师在孙悟空耳边说了一首诗，诗里有长生的秘密。
sentences.translation: The Patriarch Bodhi whispered a poem in Sun Wukong's ear, the poem contained the secret of immortality.
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure in Chinese is Subject + Verb + Object, similar to English. The measure word "首" is used for poems or songs in Chinese. The possessive particle "的" is used to indicate possession or association between two nouns.

sentences.text: 当然，我不能告诉你这首诗是什么，因为它是一个秘密。
sentences.translation: Of course, I can't tell you what this poem is because it's a secret.
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure in Chinese is Subject + Verb + Object. The measure word "首" is used before "诗" to indicate it's a poem. The word "因为" is used to introduce the reason for the action.

content.raw_text: 孙悟空听到这首诗后，每天多次读着这首诗。他记住了诗里的每一个字，他学着诗里的东西去做，他开始学习长生的秘密。

sentences.text: 孙悟空听到这首诗后，每天多次读着这首诗。
sentences.translation: After Sun Wukong heard this poem, he read this poem multiple times every day.
sentences.explanation: The structure '每天多次' means 'multiple times every day' and '读着' indicates the continuous action of reading.

sentences.text: 他记住了诗里的每一个字，他学着诗里的东西去做，他开始学习长生的秘密。
sentences.translation: He remembered every word in the poem, he learned to do things in the poem, he began to learn the secret of longevity.
sentences.explanation: The structure 学着...去做 indicates learning to do something. 长生 refers to longevity or immortality, often associated with Taoist or traditional Chinese beliefs.

content.raw_text: 但是三年后，菩提祖师对孙悟空说，“我亲爱的学生，你要小心。你已经学会了天地的秘密，但是现在你在危险中。当然，你会长生。但是五百年以后的今天，上天会给你送去雷电。要用你的智慧去避开雷电，如果不那样做你会死。雷电的五百年后，上天会给你送去火焰。要用你的智慧去避开火焰，如果不那样做你会死。火焰的五百年后，上天会给你送去大风。它会到你的头里，经过你的身体。要用你的智慧去避开大风，如果不那样做你会死。”

sentences.text: 但是三年后，菩提祖师对孙悟空说，“我亲爱的学生，你要小心。
sentences.translation: But three years later, Patriarch Bodhi said to Sun Wukong, 'My dear student, you must be careful.'
sentences.explanation: The structure '对...说' means 'said to...' in this context. The term '菩提祖师' refers to Patriarch Bodhi, a respected figure in Buddhism.

sentences.text: 你已经学会了天地的秘密，但是现在你在危险中。
sentences.translation: You have learned the secrets of heaven and earth, but now you are in danger.
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure is Subject + 已经 + Verb + 了 + Object, indicating completion of an action. The use of 在 + [location]中 is a common structure to indicate being in a certain state or condition.

sentences.text: 当然，你会长生。
sentences.translation: Of course, you will live forever.
sentences.explanation: The phrase '长生' means 'live forever' or 'immortality' in this context. It is a common theme in Chinese culture and literature.

sentences.text: 但是五百年以后的今天，上天会给你送去雷电。
sentences.translation: But five hundred years later today, heaven will send thunder and lightning to you.
sentences.explanation: The structure '会给你送去' means 'will send to you'. The use of '上天' (heaven) is a common way to refer to a higher power or fate in Chinese culture.

sentences.text: 要用你的智慧去避开雷电，如果不那样做你会死。
sentences.translation: You must use your wisdom to avoid lightning, or you will die.
sentences.explanation: This sentence emphasizes the importance of using wisdom to avoid danger. The structure '要...去...' is a common way to express the necessity of doing something in Chinese.

sentences.text: 雷电的五百年后，上天会给你送去火焰。
sentences.translation: Five hundred years after the thunder and lightning, heaven will send flames to you.
sentences.explanation: The structure '上天会给你' means 'heaven will give you', where '上天' (heaven) is the subject, '会' (will) is the auxiliary verb, and '给你' (give you) is the verb-object phrase.

sentences.text: 要用你的智慧去避开火焰，如果不那样做你会死。
sentences.translation: You must use your wisdom to avoid the flames, or you will die.
sentences.explanation: The structure 如果不那样做 (if not do that way) means 'if you don't do it that way'.

sentences.text: 火焰的五百年后，上天会给你送去大风。
sentences.translation: Five hundred years after the flames, the heavens will send a strong wind to you.
sentences.explanation: The structure '会给' indicates a future action of giving. The phrase '上天' refers to the heavens or the divine.

sentences.text: 它会到你的头里，经过你的身体。
sentences.translation: It will go into your head, through your body.
sentences.explanation: The structure '会到...经过...' indicates the action of something going into a place and passing through it.

sentences.text: 要用你的智慧去避开大风，如果不那样做你会死。
sentences.translation: You must use your wisdom to avoid the strong wind, or else you will die.
sentences.explanation: The structure 如果不那样做 (if not do that way) is a common way to express 'or else' in Chinese.
The sentence ends with a closing quotation mark.

content.raw_text: 孙悟空害怕极了，毛发都直了起来，“祖师，请帮我避开这三件事。我不会忘记你的。”

sentences.text: 孙悟空害怕极了，毛发都直了起来，“祖师，请帮我避开这三件事。
sentences.translation: Sun Wukong was extremely afraid, his hair stood on end, 'Ancestor, please help me avoid these three things.'
sentences.explanation: The sentence contains a request for help and the structure '请 + verb' which is commonly used to make polite requests in Chinese.

sentences.text: 我不会忘记你的。
sentences.translation: I will not forget you.
sentences.explanation: The structure '不会' is used to indicate the future tense, meaning 'will not'.
The sentence ends with a closing quotation mark.

content.raw_text: “别担心，”祖师说，“这个世界上没有什么事情是很难的。只有你把它想得很难。”然后，菩提祖师在孙悟空的耳边说了一个秘密。孙悟空听了以后，很快他学会了筋斗云。他一个筋斗云可以飞过十万八千里。现在他可以避开天上的雷电，火焰和大风。他可以长生了。

sentences.text: “别担心，”祖师说，这个世界上没有什么事情是很难的。
sentences.translation: Don't worry,
sentences.explanation: The structure '没有什么事情是很难的' is a common way to express 'there is nothing that is very difficult' in Chinese.

sentences.text: 只有你把它想得很难。
sentences.translation: Only you think it's difficult.
sentences.explanation: The structure '把...想得很难' is a common way in Chinese to express that someone finds something difficult to think or imagine.

words.definition: indicating the object of a verb

sentences.text: ”然后，菩提祖师在孙悟空的耳边说了一个秘密。
sentences.translation: Then, Bodhi Patriarch whispered a secret in Sun Wukong's ear.
sentences.explanation: The structure '在...的耳边说' means 'whispered in someone's ear'. The particle '了' indicates the completion of the action of telling the secret.

sentences.text: 孙悟空听了以后，很快他学会了筋斗云。
sentences.translation: After Sun Wukong listened, he quickly learned the somersault cloud.
sentences.explanation: The sentence introduces the famous ability of Sun Wukong, the Monkey King, to ride the 'somersault cloud,' a magical cloud that allows him to travel quickly through the sky.

sentences.text: 他一个筋斗云可以飞过十万八千里。
sentences.translation: He can fly over 108,000 miles with one somersault cloud.
sentences.explanation: The phrase '筋斗云' (somersault cloud) refers to a magical cloud in Chinese mythology that can carry a person through the sky. The measure word '里' is used to indicate distance in this context.

sentences.text: 现在他可以避开天上的雷电，火焰和大风。
sentences.translation: Now he can avoid the thunder, flames, and strong winds in the sky.
sentences.explanation: The structure '可以 + verb' indicates the ability to do something. The possessive particle '的' is used to indicate possession or association.

sentences.text: 他可以长生了。
sentences.translation: He can live forever.
sentences.explanation: The structure '可以 + verb' indicates the ability or permission to do something. '长生' means 'live forever' in this context.

words.definition: indicates completion or change of state

content.raw_text: 他在菩提祖师那里又住了很多年。有一天，祖师对孙悟空说，“你今天必须离开。你一直在给其他学生找麻烦。”

sentences.text: 他在菩提祖师那里又住了很多年。
sentences.translation: He lived with Bodhidharma for many years.
sentences.explanation: The structure '在...那里' means 'at/in that place'. The character '了' indicates the completion of an action.

sentences.text: 有一天，祖师对孙悟空说“你今天必须离开。
sentences.translation: One day, the patriarch said to Sun Wukong, "You must leave today."
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure follows a common pattern in Chinese where the subject is followed by the verb and then the object. The use of quotation marks indicates direct speech.

sentences.text: 你一直在给其他学生找麻烦。
sentences.translation: You have been causing trouble for other students.
sentences.explanation: The structure '在给' is used to indicate causing trouble for someone in this context.
This sentence only contains a closing quotation mark.

content.raw_text: “我应该去哪里呢？”孙悟空伤心地说。

sentences.text: “我应该去哪里呢？
sentences.translation: Where should I go?
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure is a question asking for direction. The particle '呢' is used to soften the question tone.

sentences.text: ”孙悟空伤心地说。
sentences.translation: Sun Wukong said sadly.
sentences.explanation: The structure '伤心地说' is a common way in Chinese to indicate speaking in a certain emotional manner, in this case, sadly.

content.raw_text: “回你的家，从哪里来就回哪里去。”孙悟空很伤心，一个筋斗云就离开了。

sentences.text: “回你的家，从哪里来就回哪里去。
sentences.translation: Go back to your home, go back where you came from.
sentences.explanation: This sentence emphasizes the idea of returning to where you came from. The structure '从...来就...' indicates 'from...then'.

sentences.text: ”孙悟空很伤心，一个筋斗云就离开了。
sentences.translation: Sun Wukong was very sad, and a somersault cloud left.
sentences.explanation: The sentence describes Sun Wukong feeling sad because his somersault cloud left. The use of '了' at the end of the sentence indicates the completion of the action of the cloud leaving.

content.raw_text: 他走得非常快，一个小时以后，他就回到了花果山水帘洞里的家。他听到猴子们的声音，“孩子们，我回来了，”他说。很快，很多很多的猴子跑来欢迎孙悟空。他们问，“你为什么走了？只有我们自己在这里，我们一直在等你回来。最近，这里有一个妖怪，他想要我们的山洞，他带走了我们的很多朋友。我们非常担心。但现在我们很高兴，因为我们的大王回来了。”

sentences.text: 他走得非常快，一个小时以后，他就回到了花果山水帘洞里的家。
sentences.translation: He walked very fast, and an hour later, he returned to the Water Curtain Cave in Flower Fruit Mountain.
sentences.explanation: The structure '就' in this sentence is used to indicate that the action happened earlier than expected.

words.definition: used after a verb to indicate degree or result
indicating that something happens earlier than expected

sentences.text: 他听到猴子们的声音，“孩子们，我回来了，”他说。
sentences.translation: He heard the monkeys' voices, "Children, I'm back," he said.
sentences.explanation: The sentence contains a direct speech structure with quotation marks. The word order in Chinese is different from English, with the subject usually placed before the verb.

sentences.text: 很快，很多很多的猴子跑来欢迎孙悟空。
sentences.translation: Very quickly, many many monkeys ran over to welcome Sun Wukong.
sentences.explanation: The structure '很多很多的' emphasizes the abundance of monkeys. The verb '跑来' indicates running over to a place.

sentences.text: 他们问，“你为什么走了？
sentences.translation: They asked, "Why did you leave?"
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure is a simple question in Chinese, with the question word '为什么' (why) placed before the verb '走' (leave). The particle '了' indicates the completion of the action.

sentences.text: 只有我们自己在这里，我们一直在等你回来。
sentences.translation: Only we are here, we have been waiting for you to come back.
sentences.explanation: The structure '一直在' indicates continuous action, meaning 'have been' in this context.

sentences.text: 最近，这里有一个妖怪，他想要我们的山洞，他带走了我们的很多朋友。
sentences.translation: Recently, there is a monster here who wants our cave. He took away many of our friends.
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure in Chinese is subject-verb-object, similar to English. Pay attention to the use of possessive particles '的' and the particle '了' indicating completion of an action.

sentences.text: 我们非常担心。
sentences.translation: We are very worried.
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure is subject + adverb + verb. The word '担心' means 'worried' in this context.

sentences.text: 但现在我们很高兴，因为我们的大王回来了。
sentences.translation: But now we are very happy because our king has returned.
sentences.explanation: This sentence showcases the use of possessive particle '的' to indicate possession, as well as the completion aspect marker '了' at the end of the sentence.
The sentence ends with a closing quotation mark, indicating the end of a quote or dialogue.

content.raw_text: 孙悟空很生气，“告诉我这个无法无天的妖怪。我会找到他的。”

sentences.text: 孙悟空很生气，“告诉我这个无法无天的妖怪。
sentences.translation: Sun Wukong is very angry, 'Tell me about this lawless monster.'
sentences.explanation: The sentence introduces the character Sun Wukong expressing anger and demanding information about a lawless monster. The structure '无法无天' is an idiom meaning 'unrestrained' or 'lawless'.

sentences.text: 我会找到他的。
sentences.translation: I will find him.
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure is Subject + 会 + Verb + Object + 的. The possessive particle 的 is used to indicate possession or relationship.
The sentence ends with a closing quotation mark.

content.raw_text: “他住在北面。我们不知道有多远。他来时像云，去时像风。”

sentences.text: “他住在北面。
sentences.translation: He lives in the north.
sentences.explanation: The structure '在 + location' is used to indicate where someone or something is located.

sentences.text: 我们不知道有多远。
sentences.translation: We don't know how far.
sentences.explanation: The structure '有多' is used to express 'how much/many' in this sentence.

sentences.text: 他来时像云，去时像风。
sentences.translation: When he comes, he is like a cloud; when he goes, he is like the wind.
sentences.explanation: This sentence uses similes to describe the person's behavior. The structure '来时...，去时...' means 'when he comes..., when he goes...'.
The sentence ends with a closing quotation mark.

content.raw_text: “别担心，我会找到他的。”孙悟空跳起来，一个筋斗云向北面去了，他来到了一座高山。看到了一些小妖怪，他知道这就是妖怪的家。他对小妖怪说，“我是花果山的猴王。你们的大王呢？我不想知道他的名字。他找我朋友们的麻烦，我要和他说话。”小妖怪跑进山洞里，告诉大妖怪，“外面有一只很丑的猴子。他说他是一个大王。他要和你说话。”

sentences.text: “别担心，我会找到他的。
sentences.translation: Don't worry, I will find him.
sentences.explanation: The structure 别 + verb is used to form imperatives in Chinese. 的 is a possessive particle indicating possession or relationship.

sentences.text: ”孙悟空跳起来，一个筋斗云向北面去了，他来到了一座高山。
sentences.translation: Sun Wukong jumped up, rode on a somersault cloud, and headed north to a high mountain.
sentences.explanation: This sentence introduces the character Sun Wukong and his ability to ride on a somersault cloud. The use of '了' at the end of '去了' indicates the completion of the action of heading north.

sentences.text: 看到了一些小妖怪，他知道这就是妖怪的家。
sentences.translation: Seeing some little monsters, he knew this was the monsters' home.
sentences.explanation: The structure '这就是' is a common way to say 'this is' in Chinese.

sentences.text: 他对小妖怪说，“我是花果山的猴王。
sentences.translation: He said to the little monster, 'I am the Monkey King of Flower Fruit Mountain.'
sentences.explanation: The sentence introduces the Monkey King of Flower Fruit Mountain speaking to a little monster. The structure '对...说' is a common way to indicate someone is speaking to another person.

sentences.text: 你们的大王呢？
sentences.translation: Where is your king?
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure is Subject + Possessive Particle + Noun + 呢, which is used to inquire about the whereabouts of someone or something.

words.definition: (used for emphasis or to inquire about someone's whereabouts)

sentences.text: 我不想知道他的名字。
sentences.translation: I don't want to know his name.
sentences.explanation: The structure '不想' means 'do not want' in this context. The possessive particle '的' is used to indicate possession in Chinese.

sentences.text: 他找我朋友们的麻烦，我要和他说话。
sentences.translation: He is causing trouble for my friends, I want to talk to him.
sentences.explanation: The possessive particle '的' is used to indicate possession in Chinese. In this sentence, it shows that the trouble is directed towards 'my friends'.

sentences.text: ”小妖怪跑进山洞里，告诉大妖怪，“外面有一只很丑的猴子。
sentences.translation: The little monster ran into the cave and told the big monster, 'There is a very ugly monkey outside.'
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure follows the pattern of 'subject + verb + location + action + recipient + content'. The possessive particle '的' is used to indicate the relationship between 'ugly' and 'monkey'.

sentences.text: 他说他是一个大王。
sentences.translation: He said he is a great king.
sentences.explanation: The structure '是一个' is used to indicate 'is a' in Chinese.

sentences.text: 他要和你说话。
sentences.translation: He wants to talk to you.
sentences.explanation: The structure '要...说话' is a common way to express 'want to talk' in Chinese.
The sentence ends with a closing quotation mark.

content.raw_text: 妖怪只是大笑，“我经常听到这些猴子说起他们的大王，他在外面跟祖师学习。那个大王一直不在这里。现在他已经回来了吗？”妖怪拿起他的弯刀，走出山洞，说，“花果山的大王在哪里？”

sentences.text: 妖怪只是大笑，“我经常听到这些猴子说起他们的大王，他在外面跟祖师学习。
sentences.translation: The monster just laughed, 'I often hear these monkeys talk about their great king, who is studying with the Patriarch outside.'
sentences.explanation: This sentence contains a complex structure where the monster is laughing and then quoting what the monkeys say about their king studying with the Patriarch. The possessive particle '的' is used to indicate possession.

sentences.text: 那个大王一直不在这里。
sentences.translation: The king has been away all this time.
sentences.explanation: The structure '一直不' together means 'has been away' or 'has not been here' in this context.

sentences.text: 现在他已经回来了吗？
sentences.translation: Has he come back now?
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure is Subject + Time + Verb + Particle + Question Particle.

sentences.text: ”妖怪拿起他的弯刀，走出山洞，说，“花果山的大王在哪里？
sentences.translation: The monster picked up his scimitar, walked out of the cave, and said, "Where is the Great King of Flower Fruit Mountain?
sentences.explanation: The sentence introduces a monster speaking and asking for the Great King of Flower Fruit Mountain. The use of quotation marks indicates direct speech.
The sentence consists of a closing quotation mark.

content.raw_text: “妖怪，你的眼睛很大，但怎么就没有看到我这只老猴子？”

sentences.text: “妖怪，你的眼睛很大，但怎么就没有看到我这只老猴子？
sentences.translation: Monster, your eyes are big, but how come you didn't see me, this old monkey?
sentences.explanation: The sentence uses a rhetorical question structure to express surprise or disbelief.
This sentence contains a closing quotation mark.

content.raw_text: “老猴，你很小。你为什么这样跟我说话？”

sentences.text: “老猴，你很小。
sentences.translation: Old monkey, you are very small.
sentences.explanation: The structure of this sentence is subject + adjective + noun. The word order in Chinese is different from English, so 'you are very small' in English is translated as '你很小' in Chinese.

sentences.text: 你为什么这样跟我说话？
sentences.translation: Why are you talking to me like this?
sentences.explanation: The structure '为什么...这样...' is used to ask why someone is doing something in a certain way.

sentences.translation: Chapter 2
sentences.explanation: The sentence simply indicates the chapter number, which is Chapter 2.

content.raw_text: “你什么都看不到，笨妖怪。你说我很小，但如果我想的话，我可以从天上把月亮拿下来。”

sentences.text: “你什么都看不到，笨妖怪。
sentences.translation: You can't see anything, stupid monster.
sentences.explanation: The structure '什么都' together means 'anything' or 'everything'. The word '不到' is a negation particle indicating the inability to do something.

sentences.text: 你说我很小，但如果我想的话，我可以从天上把月亮拿下来。
sentences.translation: You say I am small, but if I want to, I can take the moon down from the sky.
sentences.explanation: The structure '如果...的话' is used to express a conditional statement in Chinese. In this sentence, it means 'if I want to'.
This sentence consists of a single closing quotation mark.

content.raw_text: 妖怪大叫，他开始和孙悟空打。他们打了很长时间。妖怪用他的弯刀砍孙悟空，孙悟空马上就要输了，所以他马上从他的头上拔了几根毛发，在嘴里嚼了一下，然后把他们吐出来，变成了几百只小猴子。小猴子一起帮孙悟空打妖怪。打了一些时间，孙悟空和小猴子赢了，妖怪死了。然后孙悟空吃了毛发，小猴子又回到了孙悟空的身体里。

sentences.text: 妖怪大叫，他开始和孙悟空打。
sentences.translation: The monster roared, and he started fighting with Sun Wukong.
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure is Subject + Verb + Object. The verb '打' here means 'to fight' in this context.

sentences.text: 他们打了很长时间。
sentences.translation: They fought for a long time.
sentences.explanation: The tricky grammar structure here is the use of 了 to indicate the completion of the action of fighting.

sentences.text: 妖怪用他的弯刀砍孙悟空，孙悟空马上就要输了，所以他马上从他的头上拔了几根毛发，在嘴里嚼了一下，然后把他们吐出来，变成了几百只小猴子。
sentences.translation: The monster used his curved knife to chop Sun Wukong. Sun Wukong was about to lose, so he immediately plucked a few hairs from his head, chewed on them, then spat them out, transforming them into hundreds of little monkeys.
sentences.explanation: This sentence includes actions of transformation and quick thinking by the character Sun Wukong. The use of '马上' (immediately) emphasizes the urgency of the situation.

sentences.text: 小猴子一起帮孙悟空打妖怪。
sentences.translation: The little monkeys help Sun Wukong fight demons together.
sentences.explanation: The sentence follows a Subject-Verb-Object structure commonly seen in Chinese sentences. The tricky part for learners might be understanding the use of the verb '打' (fight) in this context, where it means 'to fight against' or 'to battle'.

sentences.text: 打了一些时间，孙悟空和小猴子赢了，妖怪死了。
sentences.translation: After some time, Sun Wukong and the little monkeys won, and the monster died.
sentences.explanation: This sentence describes a scene where Sun Wukong and the little monkeys defeated a monster after some time.

words.definition: Sun Wukong (name of the Monkey King)

sentences.text: 然后孙悟空吃了毛发，小猴子又回到了孙悟空的身体里。
sentences.translation: Then Sun Wukong ate the hair, and the little monkey returned to Sun Wukong's body.
sentences.explanation: This sentence describes a magical transformation where the little monkey returns to Sun Wukong's body after he eats a hair.

content.raw_text: 但是有些小猴子没有回到孙悟空的身体里。这些是被妖怪带来的猴子。孙悟空对他们说，“你们为什么在这里？”

sentences.text: 但是有些小猴子没有回到孙悟空的身体里。
sentences.translation: But some little monkeys did not return to Sun Wukong's body.
sentences.explanation: The structure '回到' means 'return to' and the possessive particle '的' indicates possession.

sentences.text: 这些是被妖怪带来的猴子。
sentences.translation: These are monkeys brought by monsters.
sentences.explanation: The structure '被...带来' indicates that the monkeys were brought by the monsters in a passive voice construction.

sentences.text: 孙悟空对他们说，“你们为什么在这里？
sentences.translation: Sun Wukong said to them, 'Why are you here?'
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure is Subject + Verb + Object. The use of 孙悟空 (Sun Wukong) as a name is a common practice in Chinese literature and storytelling.

words.definition: Sun (referring to 孙悟空 Sun Wukong)

sentences.explanation: The sentence ends with a closing quotation mark.

content.raw_text: 他们说，“大王走了以后，妖怪来到花果山。这两年，他经常来，带走了我们的一些猴子。你看，这里有一些从我们水帘洞里拿来的石盆和石碗！”

sentences.text: 他们说，“大王走了以后，妖怪来到花果山。
sentences.translation: They said, 'After the Great Sage Equal to Heaven left, monsters came to Flower Fruit Mountain.'
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure in Chinese is Subject-Verb-Object. The phrase '大王' refers to the Great Sage Equal to Heaven, a character from Chinese mythology. '以后' is used to indicate 'after' in this context.

sentences.text: 这两年，他经常来，带走了我们的一些猴子。
sentences.translation: These two years, he often comes and takes away some of our monkeys.
sentences.explanation: The structure '带走了' indicates that the action of taking away has been completed. The possessive particle '的' is used to indicate possession.

sentences.text: 你看，这里有一些从我们水帘洞里拿来的石盆和石碗！
sentences.translation: Look, here are some stone basins and stone bowls taken from our Water Curtain Cave!
sentences.explanation: The structure '从...里拿来' means 'taken from'. The use of '的' after a verb indicates past tense or possession.

words.definition: particle indicating past tense or possession

sentences.explanation: The sentence ends with a quotation mark followed by an ellipsis, indicating a continuation or omission of text.

content.raw_text: “大家都跟我回家，”孙悟空说。

sentences.text: “大家都跟我回家，”孙悟空说。
sentences.translation: Everyone, come back home with me,
sentences.explanation: In Chinese, the word order is different from English. The verb '说' (said) comes at the end of the sentence. Also, the use of '都' (all) emphasizes that everyone should come back home.

content.raw_text: “大王，”他们说，“我们是和妖怪一起来这里的。我们没有看到来的路，所以我们不知道怎么回家。”

sentences.text: “大王，”他们说，我们是和妖怪一起来这里的。
sentences.translation: Great king,
sentences.explanation: The structure '是...一起来' means 'came together'. The possessive particle '的' indicates possession or association.

sentences.text: 我们没有看到来的路，所以我们不知道怎么回家。
sentences.translation: We did not see the way here, so we do not know how to go home.
sentences.explanation: The structure '所以' (so) is used to indicate a cause-and-effect relationship between the first part of the sentence and the second part. '怎么' (how) is used to express the way or method of doing something.
The sentence ends with a closing quotation mark.

content.raw_text: “没问题，”孙悟空说。“我知道怎么带你们回家。你们大家都闭上眼睛，不要害怕。”

sentences.text: “没问题，”孙悟空说。
sentences.translation: No problem,
sentences.explanation: In this sentence, 孙悟空 (Sun Wukong) is a character's name. The structure of the sentence is straightforward, with the subject 孙悟空 (Sun Wukong) followed by the verb 说 (said) indicating the action of speaking.

sentences.text: “我知道怎么带你们回家。
sentences.translation: I know how to take you home.
sentences.explanation: The structure '怎么' followed by a verb indicates knowing how to do something in Chinese.

sentences.text: 你们大家都闭上眼睛，不要害怕。
sentences.translation: All of you close your eyes, don't be afraid.
sentences.explanation: The structure '都...不要' is used to emphasize that everyone should do something, in this case, close their eyes and not be afraid.
The sentence ends with a closing quotation mark.

content.raw_text: 亲爱的猴王！他把所有被妖怪带来的猴子都放在云上，一个筋斗云就回到了花果山。“张开你们的眼睛，”孙悟空说，“现在你们到家了！”

sentences.text: 亲爱的猴王！
sentences.translation: Dear Monkey King!
sentences.explanation: The phrase '亲爱的' is commonly used to address someone in a dear or beloved manner, similar to 'dear' in English.

sentences.text: 他把所有被妖怪带来的猴子都放在云上，一个筋斗云就回到了花果山。
sentences.translation: He placed all the monkeys brought by the monsters on the clouds, and with a somersault cloud, he returned to Flower Fruit Mountain.
sentences.explanation: This sentence showcases the use of the particle '把' to introduce the object of an action in Chinese grammar. It also includes the passive marker '被' and the particle '就' to indicate a sequence of events.

words.definition: particle used to introduce the object of an action

sentences.text: “张开你们的眼睛，”孙悟空说，现在你们到家了！
sentences.translation: Open your eyes,
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure in Chinese is Subject-Verb-Object. The particle '了' at the end of the sentence indicates a change of situation, in this case, arriving home.

words.definition: particle indicating completion or change of situation

sentences.explanation: This sentence consists of a closing quotation mark.

content.raw_text: 所有的猴子都很高兴。他们用酒和水果开了一个很大的宴会。孙悟空告诉了猴子们他在西大洲和南大洲的那段时间。他说，“我从祖师那里学了很多东西。现在我可以长生不死了。我现在有一个新的名字。”

sentences.text: 所有的猴子都很高兴。
sentences.translation: All the monkeys are very happy.
sentences.explanation: The possessive particle '的' is used to indicate possession or association between '猴子' (monkeys) and '所有' (all). The adverb '都' emphasizes that all the monkeys are happy.

sentences.text: 他们用酒和水果开了一个很大的宴会。
sentences.translation: They held a large banquet with wine and fruit.
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure follows the pattern of 'subject + verb + object', with the possessive particle '的' used to indicate the size of the banquet.

sentences.text: 孙悟空告诉了猴子们他在西大洲和南大洲的那段时间。
sentences.translation: Sun Wukong told the monkeys about his time in the Western and Southern Continents.
sentences.explanation: This sentence introduces the Monkey King, Sun Wukong, and his adventures in the Western and Southern Continents. Pay attention to the possessive particle '的' and the completion particle '了'.

sentences.text: 他说，“我从祖师那里学了很多东西。
sentences.translation: He said, 'I learned a lot of things from my ancestors.'
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure in Chinese is Subject-Verb-Object. The word '了' is used to indicate the completion of an action in this context.

sentences.text: 现在我可以长生不死了。
sentences.translation: Now I can live forever.
sentences.explanation: The sentence expresses the speaker's ability to live forever now.

sentences.text: 我现在有一个新的名字。
sentences.translation: I now have a new name.
sentences.explanation: The possessive particle '的' is used to indicate possession in Chinese. In this sentence, it connects '新' (new) and '名字' (name) to show that the new name belongs to the speaker.
This sentence only consists of a closing quotation mark, indicating the end of a quoted text.

content.raw_text: “你新的姓是什么，大王？”

sentences.text: “你新的姓是什么，大王？
sentences.translation: What is your new surname, Your Majesty?
sentences.explanation: The phrase '大王' is a respectful way to address someone, similar to 'Your Majesty' in English.
The sentence ends with a closing quotation mark.

content.raw_text: “我姓孙。”

sentences.text: “我姓孙。
sentences.translation: I am surnamed Sun.
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure in Chinese is Subject + Verb + Object. In this sentence, the subject is '我' (I), the verb is '姓' (surnamed), and the object is '孙' (Sun).
The sentence ends with a closing quotation mark.

content.raw_text: 所有的猴子都很高兴，说，“如果大王是老孙，我们就都是小孙。我们一家都是孙，一国都是孙，我们都住在孙姓洞里！”他们都给孙悟空拿来了好吃的水果和好酒，他们一个晚上都在唱歌跳舞，他们是幸福的一家。

sentences.text: 所有的猴子都很高兴，说，“如果大王是老孙，我们就都是小孙。
sentences.translation: All the monkeys are very happy, saying, 'If the Great King is Sun Wukong, then we are all Little Sun Wukongs.'
sentences.explanation: The sentence uses a conditional structure '如果...就...' (if...then...) and a cultural reference to the character Sun Wukong from the Chinese classic 'Journey to the West'.

sentences.text: 我们一家都是孙，一国都是孙，我们都住在孙姓洞里！
sentences.translation: Our whole family is Sun, the whole country is Sun, we all live in the Sun surname cave!
sentences.explanation: The repetition of '都是' emphasizes that everyone is from the Sun family and lives in the same place.

sentences.text: ”他们都给孙悟空拿来了好吃的水果和好酒，他们一个晚上都在唱歌跳舞，他们是幸福的一家。
sentences.translation: They all brought delicious fruits and good wine for Sun Wukong. They sang and danced all night, they are a happy family.
sentences.explanation: The sentence showcases the use of the particle '了' to indicate the completion of an action, as well as the structure '都...在' to express that an action is done by everyone in a certain place.

content.raw_text: 晚安，我亲爱的孩子。我爱你。

sentences.text: 晚安，我亲爱的孩子。
sentences.translation: Good night, my dear child.
sentences.explanation: The phrase '亲爱的' is used to express endearment towards the child, similar to saying 'dear' in English.

sentences.text: 我爱你。
sentences.translation: I love you.
sentences.explanation: This sentence is a simple declaration of love, with the subject '我' (I/me), the verb '爱' (love), and the object '你' (you).

content.raw_text: {Section_Name: 天宫里找麻烦}

sentences.text: {Section_Nam: 天宫里找麻烦}
sentences.translation: Causing trouble in the heavenly palace
sentences.explanation: The sentence describes someone causing trouble inside the heavenly palace. The word '找' can also mean 'cause' in this context.
